title: The Made-up Disease of Syndrome K
summary: Hosts Josh and Chuck tell the little-known World War II story of Syndrome K, in which doctors at a Catholic hospital on Tiber Island in Rome hid Jewish refugees during the 1943-44 Nazi occupation by pretending they had a fictitious, highly contagious Jewish disease. They cover the background of Mussolini's Italy, its colonial wars, the Lateran Treaty, Italian racial laws, the Italian surrender and German occupation, the key Nazi officers Kesselring and Kappler, the hospital's anti-fascist staff (Father Maurizio Bialek, Giovanni Borromeo, Vittorio Sacerdoti, Adriano Ossicini), the October 1943 roundup of Rome's Jews, the fates of the players, and close with a listener email from Marco.

segments.title: Opening and introduction to Syndrome K
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the story of Italian doctors saving Jews in Rome and credit listener Jesselyne Baldwin for suggesting the topic.

segments.title: Mussolini's Italy and the lead-up to World War II
segments.summary: Background on Mussolini's rise after being appointed prime minister in 1922, Italian colonial wars in Libya and Ethiopia, the 1929 Lateran Treaty creating Vatican City, and the 1938 Italian racial laws against Jews and others.

segments.title: Italy in WWII, surrender and German occupation
segments.summary: Italy's entry into the war after the Pact of Steel, Mussolini's failures, the September 1943 Italian surrender, the German occupation of Italy, and the Italian resistance.

segments.title: Nazi commanders Kesselring and Kappler
segments.summary: Description of Albert Kesselring and Herbert Kappler, the Nazi leaders in Italy, and the Ardeatine massacre in which Italians were executed in retaliation for a partisan attack.

segments.title: Tiber Island and the Fatebenefratelli hospital
segments.summary: Geography of Tiber Island and the history of the Fatebenefratelli hospital run by the Brothers of Saint John of God since the 1500s, placed between the Jewish ghetto and the Vatican.

segments.title: Anti-fascist staff at the hospital
segments.summary: Father Maurizio Bialek, the hospital administrator, and doctor Giovanni Borromeo assembled an anti-fascist staff, including Jewish doctor Vittorio Sacerdoti and volunteer Adriano Ossicini, who formed a secret committee and kept a secret radio.

segments.title: October 1943 roundup and the gold deception
segments.summary: The Nazis began rounding up Rome's Jews in October 1943, despite a deal in which the Jewish community was promised protection in exchange for fifty kilograms of gold; victims were told to bring personal items.

segments.title: The fictitious Syndrome K disease
segments.summary: The hospital staff invented Syndrome K, a fake contagious Jewish disease, to hide refugees in a separate wing. Patients wore signs, staff gave false death certificates and false papers, and a Nazi raid including a German doctor found nothing suspicious; a few Polish refugees were discovered and a radio was dumped into the river.

segments.title: Liberation and fates of the key figures
segments.summary: American troops entered Rome in June 1944. Vittorio Sacerdoti was honored by Yad Vashem in 2004; Ossicini later became a senator and died in 2019. Kesselring was convicted, died in 1960; Kappler escaped prison in 1977 with his wife's help and died there; Mussolini was executed at Lake Como and his body hung in Milan.
topics: Yad Vashem Righteous Among the Nations

segments.title: Closing remarks
segments.summary: The hosts wrap up the story, note there is a documentary titled Syndrome K, and transition to listener mail.

segments.title: Listener email from Marco
segments.summary: Marco, an Italian listener living in Rome, praises the show and gently points out that the hosts' Italian accents and pronunciation are off.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing reminder to send emails to the show and the iHeartRadio credit.
